chapter: New Orleans second line and Armstrong
title: Kid Rena and his brother
summary: The interviewer notes Rena's drummer brother, and Jackson calls Rena one of the best trumpet players with a strong upper register.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I think later his mind even went. Yeah, yeah, he had a brother named Henry Rene. He's still living, but he doesn't play anymore. Yeah, he's a drummer. He's enjoying church now or something. He's either a preacher or something. Anyway, he won't play dance either.

He's a drummer, but Rene, he was a trumpet player. He's one of the best I heard. I mean, he stayed up there in the upper register all the time. And when he was at his best, he'd give Louie, when Louie was at his best, all Louie wanted.
